p: Animal parks are at their best with little ones when you let them set the pace. Toddlers often get more excited about a duck waddling past than the animal you've walked across the park to see, so don't over-plan. A loose route, plenty of breaks and a snack stop or two will keep the day happy.

A few practical things help. Hand-washing after touching animals is important, so look out for washing stations and use them every time. A change of clothes in the car is a good idea, as is a pushchair that copes with grass and gravel. If you've got a mix of ages, let older kids lead the way to the bits they're most excited about while little ones nap or stroll.

Greenacres sits in a handy spot for the wider area. Chester Zoo, one of the UK's best-known zoos, is a short drive away for another day out, while Wepre Park in Connah's Quay is a lovely free alternative, with woodland trails, a stream and the ruins of Ewloe Castle hidden among the trees.

Hawarden, a short hop away, is a pretty village with Gladstone's Library, founded by the Victorian prime minister William Gladstone. Chester itself offers its famous city walls, the Rows and riverside walks along the Dee, so there's no shortage of ways to round off a family day. On a dry afternoon, a picnic in Wepre Park makes a cheap and cheerful finish.
